focus: Cost baseline: rank workflows by billed minutes/day and wall-clock, name top cost drivers and what each spends its time on (job-level medians); spot-check two figures against raw run JSON.
answeredQuestions: What does each workflow cost in wall-clock and runner minutes, and which workflows dominate the total?

label: Cost is concentrated: 3812 billed min/day total. spec-kit-check.yml is 1279 (33.6%), sk-doc-script-tests.yml 448 (11.8%), the top six workflows 72.5%, and twelve workflows fall in the 149-299 band or below. Twelve more workflows had zero runs in the 23.5h window, so 3812 is the push-gate baseline and any PR day adds their cost on top.

The wall-clock critical path is one serial 20-minute job. spec-kit-check median wall 1178s while its sibling jobs finish in 62s and 163s; run 39910111430 measured 1188s wall with the typecheck/test job at 1184s (99.7%). Inside that job a single step, the CLI vitest project, is 776s of 1184s (65.5%). Every push to main waits on it.

About 26% of billed minutes buy no compute: sum of median job-minutes x runs is ~2826 min/day against 3812 billed, so ~986 min/day is per-job ceil(seconds/60). Worst cases are command-tree-parity (2.3 job-min billed as 4, 42% efficiency) and dispatch-enforcement-guard (2.3 billed as 4, 41%). Consolidating small jobs cannot recover this, because the ceiling applies per job and serialising 70s legs into one ~540s job worsens wall-clock.

Fixed per-job overhead dominates: every job in run 39910111430 spends 50-51s in actions/checkout. The push fan-out is ~21 jobs across 14 workflows per push, at ~73 pushes/day that is ~1500 job starts and ~1250 min/day of checkout alone (~33% of billed). For the smallest gates checkout is the job: markdown-link-integrity's 59s job leaves ~9s of link checking behind a ~50s clone.

Cost scales with push count, not with code changed: twelve push-triggered workflows each recorded exactly 73 runs in 23.5h with push:40/success:40 in their last 40 events, so the repo takes ~73 pushes/day to main and each starts ~13 workflows holding ~21 jobs (~58 billed min per full fan-out). Push frequency, not per-push work, sets the bill.

trigger-index-rebuild.yml's recorded 0s job medians and 0 billed minutes are a measurement artifact, not a free workflow: run 39912381915 is conclusion skipped with both jobs skipped at the same timestamp and empty steps, and job medians are taken from the 5 latest completed runs. Any cost ranking built from this dataset understates the rebuild workflow by construction; its real cost is the fan-out it causes, not its own runtime.

Roughly a third of gate traffic may be re-gating auto-generated index commits: trigger-index-rebuild shows skipped:20 success:20 over its last 40 runs, and spec-kit-check recorded 50 runs against 73 for its peers, consistent with one path filter already excluding index-only commits. If the other twelve push gates lack that filter, ~23 of 73 push runs are index-only commits worth ~700-800 billed min/day of the ~2533 attributable to those twelve. INFERRED: needs the paths: blocks in gate-inputs.yml, message-contract.yml and peers.

Documented contradiction: README.md says a newer commit pushed with the default GITHUB_TOKEN starts no run, but 20 of the last 40 trigger-index-rebuild runs are skipped by the Trigger-Index-Rebuild: ci trailer guard, and a skip requires a run to have started. Most likely resolution (inferred) is that the push job authenticates with a token that does start runs and the GITHUB_TOKEN sentence describes a degraded fallback. Recorded for a later iteration; no halt raised, no operator present.

Overengineering and flakiness already visible in the cost data: advisory-checks is documented as reports-without-gating yet spends 75 billed min/day across 73 runs, with a 60s job whose cost is 100% avoidable if it moves to a scheduled lane; deep-loop-runtime fails 13 of its last 40 runs (32.5%) at 11.5 min per run; diagram-corpus fails 12 of 40; strict-pass-freshness-report is the dataset's most expensive single run at 2577s wall / 2568s job / 43 billed min, again one serial job.

direction: Consolidating the small sub-140s workflows into fewer jobs to recover billing-floor waste
reason: Billed minutes are ceil per job. Merging two 70s parallel jobs into one job bills ceil(140/60)=3 instead of 2+2=4, saving 1 min but serialising the legs and roughly doubling that workflow's wall-clock. The saving is smaller than the wall-clock loss and does not touch the dominant costs (spec-kit-check, 26% rounding floor, checkout overhead).

direction: Treating trigger-index-rebuild.yml's 0 billed minutes as evidence it is cost-free
reason: Run 39912381915 shows the sampled runs are skipped with empty steps, so the job medians are artifacts. The workflow's cost is the fan-out it triggers, not its own runtime.
